'''Raymond Spalding''' (born March 11, 1997) is an American basketball player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]].

==High school career==
Spalding is the son of Raymond Brooks and Gerri and grew up playing soccer, kickball, and basketball.<ref name="dream">{{cite news|last1=Greer|first1=Jeff|title=Louisville basketball's Ray Spalding is chasing his dream of being a household name in his hometown|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2017/12/27/ray-spalding-louisville-cardinals-basketball-nba-draft/944726001/|accessdate=May 13, 2018|work=[[Louisville Courier-Journal]]|date=December 27, 2017}}</ref> He attended [[Trinity High School (Louisville)|Trinity High School]] in [[Louisville, Kentucky]], where he was coached by Mike Szabo.<ref name="greer">{{cite news|last1=Greer|first1=Jeff|title=Ray Spalding announces he'll leave Louisville, stay in the NBA draft pool|url=https://www.courier-journal.com/story/sports/college/louisville/2018/04/03/ray-spalding-announces-hell-leave-louisville-stay-nba-draft-pool/481775002/|accessdate=May 13, 2018|work=[[Louisville Courier Journal]]|date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> Spalding began to receive college looks after scoring 34 points in an AAU tournament the summer before his senior year of high school. He committed to [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] because he wanted to become a household name in his hometown.<ref name="dream"/>

==College career==
Spalding came off the bench his first two years at Louisville. He averaged 5.9 points and 5.7 rebounds per game as a sophomore.<ref>{{cite news|title=No. 2 Midwest seed Louisville draws familiar foe in first round|url=http://www.kentucky.com/sports/college/acc/university-of-louisville/article138088423.html|accessdate=May 13, 2018|work=[[Lexington Herald-Leader]]|date=March 12, 2017}}</ref> After the season, Spalding noticed the work teammate [[Donovan Mitchell]] put in to become an NBA player and resolved to do the same. He pulled down a career-high 16 rebounds to go with 21 points in a win versus [[Grand Canyon Antelopes men's basketball|Grand Canyon]] in December 2017.<ref name="dream"/> Spalding had a career-high 23 points to go with 12 rebounds in a 82-78 double overtime win over [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish men's basketball|Notre Dame]] on January 16, 2018.<ref>{{cite news|title=Spalding scores 23, Louisville beats Notre Dame 82-78 in 2OT|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=400986207|accessdate=May 13, 2018|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]|date=January 16, 2018}}</ref> He moved into the starting lineup as a junior, averaging 12.3 points, 8.6 rebounds, 1.7 blocks and 1.5 steals per game. Spalding led the team to a 22-14 season and the quarterfinals of the NIT.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Johnson|first1=Raphielle|title=Louisville forward Ray Spalding to enter 2018 NBA Draft|url=https://collegebasketball.nbcsports.com/2018/04/03/louisville-forward-ray-spalding-to-enter-2018-nba-draft/|accessdate=May 13, 2018|work=[[NBC Sports]]|date=April 3, 2018}}</ref> He was an Honorable Mention All-[[Atlantic Coast Conference]] selection. After the season, Spalding entered the [[2018 NBA draft]] and hired an agent, thus forgoing his final season at Louisville.<ref name="greer" />
